summary: A draft that adds a read-only Neutron Networks BFF (`list`, `getById`, subnets) and a Networks list and detail page behind a new `networks` nav key. CI is green, but one bug blocks the merge: `list` forwards `project_id` to Neutron, so shared and external networks the user can see are hidden ([[ref:c15]]). The PR also duplicates the open draft #1385 ([[ref:c13]]), which needs settling before either one merges. Against issue #1019 the PR meets 2 of 8 acceptance criteria, partly meets 4, leaves the permission criterion out of scope and doesn't meet the testing one (no tests for the router, helpers or components). The rest are client-side standards nits.
index_affected: Network BFF: new `network.networks` router (`list`, `getById`, subnets), helpers and Zod types; client routes `/projects/$projectId/network/networks` list and `$networkId` detail; `networks` nav key in `buildNavSections`.

c15.issue: `networks.list` sends `project_id` to Neutron, so shared and external networks are hidden
c15.title: `list` filters by `project_id`, hiding shared and external networks
c15.explanation:
`list` takes out only `searchTerm` and `status` from its input, so `project_id` (required by `projectScopedInputSchema`, `packages/aurora/src/server/trpc.ts:144`) stays in `openstackFilters` and goes to Neutron as a query filter at `packages/aurora/src/server/Network/routers/networksRouter.ts:42`. The [Neutron list-networks reference](https://docs.openstack.org/api-ref/network/v2/#list-networks) says the default policy returns the project's own networks *and* networks shared with it. With `project_id=<id>` in the query, only owned networks come back. Shared tenant networks and external/provider networks owned by another project (usually the ones users attach to) never show up in the list.

The security-group router already solves the same problem: `packages/aurora/src/server/Network/routers/securityGroupRouter.ts:83` fetches own (`project_id`, `shared: false`) and `packages/aurora/src/server/Network/routers/securityGroupRouter.ts:84` fetches shared (`shared: true`), then merges them. The comment at `packages/aurora/src/server/Network/routers/securityGroupRouter.ts:82` explains why simply dropping `project_id` is wrong too: an admin token would then get every project's resources (#1321). No test covers what `list` sends.
c15.fix: Follow `securityGroupRouter`: fetch owned (`project_id`, `shared=false`) and shared (`shared=true`) networks (plus `router:external=true` if external networks should be listed), merge them by `id`, and add a router test that checks the query parameters.

c1.issue: Detail page fetches the same network twice (loader `getById.query` + component `getById.useQuery`)
c1.title: The network is fetched twice on every detail visit
c1.explanation: The `$networkId` loader calls `network.networks.getById.query` at `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/$networkId.tsx:124`, but uses the result only for the page title. `RouteComponent` then requests the same input again through `trpcReact.network.networks.getById.useQuery`, so every detail visit makes two identical requests. copilot-instructions A.3 asks for page-critical data to come from the loader.
c1.fix: Return the network from the loader and read it with `Route.useLoaderData()`, or seed the query cache from the loader (`ensureQueryData`) so `useQuery` doesn't refetch.

c13.issue: Duplicates open draft PR #1385 (same Networks BFF + pages); 9 non-generated files conflict
c13.title: Same work as open draft PR #1385
c13.explanation: Open draft #1385 adds the same Neutron Networks BFF and read-only list/detail pages: `networksRouter.ts`, `types/network.ts`, `networkHelpers.ts`, `NetworksList.tsx`, `NetworkDetailsView.tsx`, the routes and the nav entry. Whichever PR merges second runs into real conflicts in 9 non-generated files. #1385 also has a changeset, a design doc (`docs/0017_networks_bff.md`) and tests for the router, helpers, types and components, all of which this PR lacks. Neither the PR body nor the discussion mentions #1385.
c13.fix: Agree with the author of #1385 which PR goes forward, and close the other or reduce it to whatever it adds on top.

c2.issue: 401/403 on the detail page render an inline error instead of a Sign-in redirect or a page-level info Message
c2.title: 401/403 handled inline on the detail page
c2.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/$networkId.tsx:65` maps `FORBIDDEN` and `UNAUTHORIZED` to descriptions that `NetworkLoadError` shows in the page. copilot-instructions B.6 asks for a redirect to Sign-in on 401 and a page-level info Message on 403. The `_auth` layout checks the session too, so in practice this mostly matters for a token that expires mid-session.
c2.fix: On `UNAUTHORIZED`, redirect to Sign-in the way other routes do; on `FORBIDDEN`, show the page-level info Message.

c3.issue: 401 copy says "Log in again to continue."; the writing rules require "Sign in"
c3.title: "Log in" wording in the 401 message
c3.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/$networkId.tsx:66` reads "The session has expired. Log in again to continue." copilot-instructions B.19 and the Quick Reject list require "Sign in", not "Log in".
c3.fix: Change the string to use "Sign in" and re-extract the catalogs (`pnpm check-i18n`).

c4.issue: Raw `<button>` for "Try Again" in the subnets error state instead of Juno `Button`
c4.title: Raw `<button>` where Juno `Button` exists
c4.explanation: The subnets error `Status` at `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkDetailsView.tsx:69` uses a plain `<button onClick={() => refetch()}>`, so it gets no Juno styling or variant. copilot-instructions B.1 and the Quick Reject list reject raw HTML controls where a Juno equivalent exists. `$networkId.tsx` in this PR already uses Juno `Button`.
c4.fix: Use Juno `Button` (for example `variant="primary"`) with the same `onClick`.

c6.issue: Active detail tab is kept in `useState`, not in the URL search params
c6.title: Detail tab is lost on refresh
c6.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkDetailsView.tsx:109` keeps the active tab in `useState`, so a refresh or a shared link always opens Overview. copilot-instructions B.9 lists "Active tab" as state that must live in the URL (`tab`).
c6.fix: Add a `tab` search param to the `$networkId` route's `validateSearch` and read and write it with `useSearch`/`navigate`.

c7.title: `PopupMenu` without the required `PopupMenuToggle`
c7.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkTableRow.tsx:56` renders `<PopupMenu><PopupMenuOptions>` with the default toggle, and `PopupMenuToggle` isn't imported. copilot-instructions B.14 requires `<PopupMenuToggle as="div"><Button icon="moreVert" /></PopupMenuToggle>` as the trigger, for a consistent accessible button.
c7.fix: Wrap the trigger in `<PopupMenuToggle as="div"><Button icon="moreVert" /></PopupMenuToggle>`, as the other list rows do.

c8.issue: Network status is shown as plain text instead of a `Badge`
c8.title: Status without a `Badge`
c8.explanation: The list row at `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkTableRow.tsx:43` renders `network.status` as plain text, and the detail Overview at `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkDetailsView.tsx:116` does the same. copilot-instructions B.1 asks for status indicators to use `Badge`.
c8.fix: Render the status as a Juno `Badge` with a variant that matches the state (for example success for `ACTIVE`, danger for `ERROR`).

c9.issue: Admin state is shown as all-caps `UP` / `DOWN`
c9.title: All-caps admin state strings
c9.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkTableRow.tsx:46` and `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkDetailsView.tsx:117` translate `admin_state_up` as `` t`UP` `` / `` t`DOWN` ``. copilot-instructions B.19 says text is never all-caps.

c10.issue: Labels "Created At" / "Updated At" capitalise the preposition
c10.title: Title case: "Created At" / "Updated At"
c10.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkDetailsView.tsx:132` and the next line use `` t`Created At` `` and `` t`Updated At` ``. copilot-instructions B.19 keeps short prepositions like "at" lowercase in title case.

c11.title: Prop-to-state sync through `useEffect`
c11.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/network/networks/-components/NetworkListContainer.tsx:36` runs `setInputPage(currentPage.toString())` in a `useEffect` whenever `currentPage` changes. That costs an extra render per page change, and copilot-instructions A.1 asks to flag such syncs.
c11.fix: Derive the value during render (keep the previous prop in state and reset when it changes), or remount the input with `key={currentPage}`.

c16.issue: `list` ignores Neutron pagination (`limit`/`marker`, next links), so a capped deployment silently truncates
c16.title: No pagination on the Neutron networks list
c16.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/server/Network/routers/networksRouter.ts:44` makes one `GET /v2.0/networks` call with no `limit`/`marker`, and the response schema has no `networks_links`. The [Neutron pagination reference](https://docs.openstack.org/api-ref/network/v2/#pagination) says a deployment can cap list size, and then returns next links. With such a cap, only the first page arrives, with no sign it was cut, and the client-side search, status filter and page count work only on that page. By default (pagination off) Neutron returns everything, so this only hits deployments that enable it.
c16.fix: Follow `networks_links` `next` until it runs out (or page with `limit`/`marker`) and add `networks_links` to the response schema.

c17.issue: `NetworkSortKeySchema` allows `shared`, which isn't a documented Neutron network sort key
c17.title: `shared` is not a Neutron sort key
c17.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/server/Network/types/network.ts:61` allows `name`, `status`, `admin_state_up` and `shared`, under a comment saying they're supported by Neutron. The [list-networks reference](https://docs.openstack.org/api-ref/network/v2/#list-networks) limits sort keys to `admin_state_up`, `availability_zone_hints`, `id`, `mtu`, `name`, `status`, `tenant_id`, `project_id`. `sort_key=shared` is forwarded as-is, so Neutron may reject the request or ignore the sort. The UI doesn't offer this sort today, so nothing breaks yet.
c17.fix: Remove `shared` from the enum (or sort by it in the BFF) and correct the comment.

c24.issue: No tests for the new router, helpers or components (issue #1019 asks for complete testing coverage)
c24.title: New BFF and pages ship without tests
c24.explanation: Issue #1019 lists complete testing coverage (unit, integration, E2E) among its acceptance criteria. The PR adds no tests for `networksRouter.ts`, `networkHelpers.ts`, the types or any new component; only `buildNavSections.test.ts` changed. The "I have added tests" box in the PR body is unticked. The `project_id` bug in [[ref:c15]] is the kind of thing a router test checking the query parameters would catch.
c24.fix: Add vitest tests for the router (query parameters, error mapping), the helpers and the list/detail components, following the existing `securityGroupRouter.test.ts` and route tests.

c25.issue: Project home page has no Networks card, though the sidebar now has a Networks entry
c25.title: Networks missing from the project home cards
c25.explanation: `packages/aurora/src/client/routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/index.tsx:87` and the cards around it build Network cards for security groups, floating IPs and routers, gated by `isEnabled`, but there's none for `networks`. `buildNavSections` now adds Networks to the sidebar, so the home page and the sidebar disagree.
c25.fix: Add a Networks card gated by `isEnabled("networks")` next to the other Network cards.

c26.issue: The new `networks` service key isn't documented in the README or `.env.example` key lists
c26.title: `networks` service key not documented
c26.explanation: The PR gates the new nav entry with `isEnabled("networks")`, which makes `networks` part of the public `enabledServices` contract. The service-key lists in `packages/aurora/README.md:183` and `packages/aurora/README.md:210` (the source of truth for `AuroraApp` props) and the comment at `apps/dashboard/.env.example:11` don't include it. An operator who sets `VITE_ENABLED_SERVICES` from the documented list hides the new Networks page without knowing. `routers` was already missing from these lists.
c26.fix: Add `networks` (and the missing `routers`) to both README lists and the `.env.example` comment.

edge_cases: Project that uses a shared or external network owned by another project (e.g. the provider `public` network): it doesn't appear in the Networks list, because `list` sends `project_id` to Neutron ([[ref:c15]]).
Admin token on the Networks list: check that only the project's own and shared networks are listed, not every project's ([[ref:c15]]).
A `list` call with `sort_key=shared`: Neutron rejects it or ignores the sort ([[ref:c17]]).

fixes.new: `list` forwards `project_id`, `name`, `admin_state_up`, `shared`, `sort_key` and `sort_dir` to Neutron (everything except `searchTerm` and `status`).
